headline: Shoreperf's dead trend is alive — and silence now gets named
lede: The perf nightly had been cancelling at scheduling every night since Nov 6: GitHub retired the macos-14 image under us. It runs on macos-26 now, prints its image onto every trend point, and the shift report grew a voice for exactly this failure shape — silent nights.

notes.text: Shoreperf nightly back on the air (PR #2096, #2054): macos-26 provisions, all three profiles land numbers (desktop 14.0 / qhd 12.2 / phone 21.4 fps on Apple Metal), and every run stamps its runner image into the summary so a level shift at the image seam reads as the runner, not the code.

The shift report now speaks silent nights: any nightly-family workflow whose scheduled runs all cancel (>=2) is named in the CI section with its night count. Six dead shoreperf nights went unmentioned last week — machinery that goes quiet is machinery that's dead.

Answered why Jon's #2053 smoke went red at 'VPad boot': nothing to do with runners. Since the consent gate landed (#1733), vpadboot's generic start ladder can't get past the consent dialog on /gauntlet — filed with instrumented evidence and a proposed fix for QA (#2095).

New CI tripwire: no workflow may pin a retired macOS label (macos-14/13/12). A dead label never fails loudly — it cancels every scheduled run quietly — so now the checker refuses it at review time instead.
